state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Great job starting to identify the net of a 3D shape! Let's focus on breaking down the shape into its individual faces. Can you try to identify the individual shapes that make up the net you have drawn? Remember, each face of the net corresponds to a 2D shape.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, okay... so I can see there's a circle and then like a curved bit next to it? Is the curved bit a sector? I'm still not really sure how those pieces fold up into a 3D shape though - like, which way do they go?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with identifying the circle and sector in the net! To visualize how they fold up into a 3D shape, think about how each face will connect to form the complete shape. Try folding along the edges of each shape in the net to see how they fit together in space.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: So like... if I fold the sector up, does it curve round to make the side of the shape, and then the circle goes on top or bottom to close it off? I'm trying to imagine it but I'm still a bit confused about which way the curved edge of the sector connects to the circle - does it match up all the way round?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher gives generic advice about identifying faces and folding without addressing the specific visualization struggle, and while the student shows some progress in imagining the cone formation, they remain confused about the fundamental connection between the sector's arc length and circle's circumference.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher breaks down the problem into manageable steps (identifying shapes, then folding) and provides encouragement, but offers limited scaffolding when the student explicitly asks for help visualizing the connection between shapes in Turn 4, missing an opportunity to adjust support level to the student's demonstrated need.
